mcqs.question: What expression gives the limiting (maximum static) frictional force between two dry surfaces?
mcqs.explanation: Limiting friction is the greatest value that static friction can attain before motion starts. It is given by f_{max}=\mu_s N, where \mu_s is the coefficient of static friction and N is the normal reaction. Option B is kinetic friction, C is just the normal force, and D would imply no friction, which is incorrect.

mcqs.question: A block of mass 1 kg slides on a horizontal surface with a coefficient of kinetic friction 0.2. What is the magnitude of the kinetic friction force acting on the block? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: The normal reaction N = mg = 1 kg × 10 m/s² = 10 N. Kinetic friction f_k = \mu_k N = 0.2 × 10 N = 2 N. Option B uses the coefficient alone, C multiplies incorrectly, and D would mean no friction, which is not the case.

mcqs.question: How is the coefficient of friction defined for two dry surfaces in contact?

options.A: Ratio of the frictional force to the normal force
options.B: Product of the frictional force and the normal force
options.C: Difference between the frictional force and the normal force
options.D: Mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration

mcqs.answer: Ratio of the frictional force to the normal force
mcqs.explanation: The coefficient of friction (static \mu_s or kinetic \mu_k) is a dimensionless number defined as \mu = f / N, where f is the frictional force and N is the normal reaction. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated quantities.

mcqs.question: A block rests on an inclined plane. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is 0.4. What is the smallest angle of the incline (in degrees) at which the block will just start to slide? (Use g = 10 m/s² and take tan⁻¹(0.4) ≈ 21.8°)
mcqs.explanation: The block begins to slide when the component of gravity down the plane equals the maximum static friction: mg sinθ = μ_s mg cosθ ⇒ tanθ = μ_s. Hence θ = tan⁻¹(0.4) ≈ 21.8°. The other angles are larger and would also cause sliding, but the question asks for the smallest angle.

mcqs.question: A 5 kg block is pulled horizontally with a force of 30 N on a rough surface where the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.3. What is the acceleration of the block? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Normal reaction N = mg = 5 × 10 = 50 N. Kinetic friction f_k = μ_k N = 0.3 × 50 = 15 N. Net force = 30 N – 15 N = 15 N. Acceleration a = F_net / m = 15 N / 5 kg = 3 m/s². Options B and C arise from arithmetic errors, D would imply the forces balance, which they do not.

mcqs.question: A crate initially at rest on a floor is pulled by a steadily increasing horizontal force. Which type of friction acts on the crate before it starts moving and after it starts moving?

options.A: Static friction before motion and kinetic friction after motion
options.B: Kinetic friction before motion and static friction after motion
options.C: Static friction both before and after motion
options.D: Kinetic friction both before and after motion

mcqs.answer: Static friction before motion and kinetic friction after motion
mcqs.explanation: While the crate is stationary, static friction opposes the applied force up to its maximum value. Once the applied force exceeds this limit, the crate moves and kinetic friction takes over. Options B, C, and D contradict the definitions of static and kinetic friction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about limiting (maximum static) friction is correct?

options.A: Limiting friction equals the maximum value of static friction
options.D: Limiting friction is always greater than kinetic friction

mcqs.answer: Limiting friction equals the maximum value of static friction
mcqs.explanation: Limiting friction is defined as the greatest possible static friction force before motion begins, i.e., f_{max}=\mu_s N. It is not equal to kinetic friction (B), it is not zero (C), and while it is often larger than kinetic friction, it is not guaranteed to be always greater (D) because the coefficients can be equal in special cases.

mcqs.question: Two blocks are placed one over the other on a horizontal surface. The top block has mass 2 kg, the bottom block 5 kg. The coefficient of static friction between the blocks is 0.5, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the bottom block and the ground is 0.3. A horizontal force of 20 N is applied to the top block. Will the top block slide over the bottom block? (Take g = 10 m/s²)

options.A: The top block will slide over the bottom block
options.B: Both blocks will move together without slipping
options.C: Both blocks will remain at rest
options.D: The situation cannot be determined with the given data

mcqs.answer: Both blocks will move together without slipping
mcqs.explanation: Maximum static friction between the blocks: f_{s,max}=μ_s N = 0.5 × (2 kg × 10 m/s²)=10 N. If both blocks move together, the system mass is 7 kg, so acceleration a = 20 N / 7 kg ≈ 2.86 m/s². The force needed to accelerate the top block is m_top a ≈ 5.7 N, which is less than the 10 N available from static friction, so no slipping occurs. Hence they move together. Option A assumes slipping, C ignores the applied force, and D is false because the data are sufficient.
